incident-bot: [INCIDENT - Sev2] Serving errors detected for hosted generation and streaming endpoints. Alerting oncall @Alex P. — increased 5xx rate and failed streaming sessions. Runbook: https://redwood-runbooks.internal/serving-5xx

Alex P.: acked. I'm on it. Seeing a spike of 5xx from model-serving-proxy cluster - likely around kernel selection path. Pulling logs and tailing stderr. Will correlate deploys. Can someone mute noisy alerts to avoid paging spam?

Jamal S.: confirmed multiple customer tickets about interrupted streams. Which customers are in the error set? any SLA hits yet?

Alex P.: early look: 3 tenants (AcmeCorp, BetaApps, DataLeaf) show elevated error logs - tokenization failures followed by OOMs on some pods. Quick mitigation: I'll divert traffic to model-v1.3-fallback (90% primary -> 10% fallback then increase) to reduce pressure. Also going to flush KV cache for node-group-7.

Tess L.: oncall handover: I'm taking the next shift in ~20m. Alex — please add a short state update here (mitigation + next steps) so I can pickup and push statuspage update.

Alex P.: applied traffic split to model-v1.3-fallback (traffic split command executed). Flushed KV cache on node-group-7. Observed 5xx rate drop from ~28% -> ~4% within ~5m. Rolling back the runtime kernel change is still on the table but not yet executed — want to see stability after split. Muted non-critical alerts.

Maria G.: CSMs briefed. Rachel — can you draft a customer-facing note? Keep it short, with impact + mitigation + next steps + offer for follow-up.

Rachel C.: Drafting now — pasting a working version below for review: 

```
Hi <Customer name>,

We want to let you know we experienced elevated error rates for text generation and streaming on the Redwood hosted API between 2026-03-15 07:12 UTC and 2026-03-15 07:46 UTC. During that window some requests returned 5xx errors or had interrupted streams. Affected customers include AcmeCorp, BetaApps, and DataLeaf.

What we did: diverted traffic to a stable model variant (model-v1.3-fallback) and flushed an internal cache to reduce pressure. We completed a rollback of the recent runtime kernel change at 07:46 UTC which normalized requests.

Next steps: we are preparing a detailed RCA and preventative actions; we will follow up with a timeline and a short post-incident summary within 48 hours. If you want a dedicated sync to discuss impact on your traffic please reply to this message and we'll schedule.

We apologize for the disruption — Rachel (CSM) on behalf of Redwood Inference
```

Alex P.: rollback started at 07:40 UTC, completed at 07:46 UTC. After rollback error rates are back within normal bounds (~0.2%-0.5%). Confirming metrics and logs for a 30m post-rollback window.

Alex P.: quick timeline snippet (for the RCA):

```
07:11 UTC - runtime v2.9.1 deployed to serving cluster
07:12 UTC - first alerts: spike in 5xx and streaming disconnects
07:15 UTC - oncall paged (Alex P.)
07:18 UTC - traffic split to model-v1.3-fallback applied
07:22 UTC - KV cache flush on node-group-7
07:30 UTC - error rate reduced substantially
07:40 UTC - rollback of kernel selection change initiated
07:46 UTC - rollback complete; metrics normalized
08:10 UTC - customer & internal comms drafted
```

Tess L.: thanks. I'll post a short statuspage update and push the customer note once we have final impact numbers. Suggested statuspage line: 

"Resolved — Elevated error rates impacting hosted generation/streaming noticed 07:12 UTC, mitigated 07:46 UTC. Detailed RCA to follow."

Maria G.: please also prepare an internal exec summary template with the high-level impact (# of tenants affected, estimated SLA exposure, any data exfil concerns). Security — any flags?

Jamal S.: SLA/impact check: based on request counts for the window we estimate ~0.08% of total tokens generated were affected; three tenants had >1% of their requests retried. Need confirmation from billing metrics but appears below immediate contractual breach thresholds; we'll quantify.

Rachel C.: final customer follow-up draft (short RCA + invite): 

```
Hi <Customer name>,

Summary: between 2026-03-15 07:12–07:46 UTC you may have seen intermittent 5xx errors or interrupted streams for text generation requests. Root cause: a runtime kernel selection change that did not handle long-prefix batching correctly, causing OOMs in a subset of pods.

What we did: diverted traffic to a stable model variant, flushed an internal KV cache, and rolled back the runtime change. Full service returned to normal at 07:46 UTC.

What we're doing next: 1) Add canary gating to kernel selection deployments, 2) add alerting for prefix-related OOMs, 3) tighten per-tenant fallback routing and automatic retries.

If you'd like a dedicated post-incident call please reply and we will schedule. We regret the disruption and are committed to preventing recurrence.

Best,
Rachel C. (CSM)
```

Alex P.: final checks: logs corroborate the kernel-selection path as root cause; no customer data was exposed. I'll send the raw error-sample snippets to the postmortem doc.

Tess L.: I'll publish the statuspage update now and set a reminder to create an RCA doc in 24 hours for the incident review board. Also please add recommended owners for the preventative actions: runtime team for canary gating, infra for KV cache instrumentation, serving-runtime for fallback enforcement.

incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED at 2026-03-15 08:15 UTC — severity downgraded to post-incident review.

Maria G.: thanks everyone. I'll assemble the internal exec summary and route the customer templates out. Alex/Tess — please add timeline clarifications to the RCA doc (links pls).

Jamal S.: noted, will follow up on SLA numbers and include in the exec note.

Rachel C.: sending the customer notes out now to the impacted accounts and will offer a follow-up call.

Alex P.: closing loop — I'll post a link to the RCA draft in this thread when ready.

Tess L.: thanks all. Great job on fast mitigation and clear comms. :thumbsup:
